newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares up as investors bargain-hunt.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares up as investors bargain-hunt.

text.p: Bargain-hunting investors helped push up Egyptian share prices on Sunday, with low-priced cement and milling firms dominating the market.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) all-share index rose 0.72 points to close at 398.58 points from 397.86 on Thursday in average turnover of 79.05 million pounds ($23.28 million).
"The market was selective today. When it went down a few weeks ago, some share prices went down too far," said Mohammed Abdullah, partner in Intercapital brokerage.
Egyptian Financial and Industrial (EFIC) was the day's most active share, closing 6.00 higher at 206 after shares worth more than 6.30 million pounds changed hands.

Abdullah said the fertiliser stock was gaining strength on rumours that it planned to take over another fertiliser company. He said there were also reports EFIChad improved the quality of its products with an eye to exporting abroad.
Cement firms traded actively, with investors buying up the cheapest stocks in the successful sector, Abdullah said.

Helwan Portland Cement topped the cement sector, trading in more than 5.90 million pounds but ended unchanged at 80. Egyptian Tora Portland Cement lost 0.70 pounds to close at 95.50 but traded in more than 4.20 million pounds.
Amriyah Cement gained 1.01 pounds to close at 88.00 after 3.40 million pounds changed hands.

Two milling firms made the top 10 most active. Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose by 4.40 pounds to 92.40 after trading in more than 5.50 million pounds while North Cairo Flour Mills gained 1.50 pounds after more than 3.30 million pounds changed hands.
Misr Free Shops rose 0.50 pounds to 47.00 after trading in more than 3.70 million pounds.
The firm, which has a monopoly on duty-free shops in Egypt, announced good results for the first half of the 1996/7 financial year.
The government sold off 66.8 percent of the 3.5 million shares in the company through the stock exchange in January.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 656.16 from 653.22 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 265.00 from 264.99.
Out of the 82 shares traded, 34 gained, 26 lost and 22 ended the day unchanged.
